issue.title: Agent-delta authored_local_request nests fork ancestry and grows toward the 256 KiB capture cap, dead-ending long monitor sessions
issue.description:
## What is wrong

`persist_agent_delta` (`src/sase/continuation_capture/agent_delta.py`) records the prepared prompt's `authored_local_request`, which is the *`#fork`-expanded* step prompt (`authored_local_request=step_prompt` in `src/sase/macro/workflow_executor_steps_prompt_prepare.py`). For a session member launched with `#fork:<prev>`, that text begins with `# Previous Continuation` and contains the parent's whole replay. Replay (`src/sase/history/chat_fork/continuation/_render.py::_render_agent_delta`) then renders that authored text as the parent's `### User` block, so each member's authored request nests all prior ancestry and grows linearly with session length.

The Rust validator caps the field: `validate_agent_delta` -> `validate_non_empty_text(.., "authored_local_request", MAX_TEXT_BYTES)` with `MAX_TEXT_BYTES = 256 * 1024` (`sase-core crates/sase_core/src/continuation/schema.rs`). Once a session's expanded prompt passes 256 KiB, agent-delta capture fails with `authored_local_request is too large`, the member gets no continuation node, and its next monitor result settles `not-launchable` ("monitor result is missing its exact starter parent node"), the same dead-end seen in bob-cli-bc.4 (that one was triggered by ANSI control bytes instead).

## Evidence (2026-10-24)

- bob-cli-bc.4 session: authored_local_request bytes per member --1..--5 = 11109, 19896, 29312, 34905, 43360; raw prompts were only 3-7 KB each. Every authored request starts with `# Previous Continuation`.
- Session `50` (sase) reached 126,224 bytes at member `50--g`; `sase-1m3.7.1.5--6` reached 113,506 bytes. 2,117 October prepared prompts scanned: none over 200 KiB yet, so this is latent, at roughly half the cap.
- The continuation prompt budget is 800,000 bytes (`continuation_budget_prompt_budget_bytes`), well above the 256 KiB authored cap, so budget reduction does not keep long sessions under it.

## Repro

Run a monitor-driven agent session (agent -> `sase monitor start` -> follow-up -> ...) for enough members that the materialized follow-up prompt exceeds 256 KiB. Then check `<artifacts>/continuation/capture_errors.jsonl` for `authored_local_request is too large` and the next monitor's `done.json` for `monitor_followup_outcome: not-launchable`.

## Decide during planning

Either capture only the local (pre-fork-expansion) request and have replay walk the parent chain instead of relying on nested authored text, or bound the authored field (for example, store it by text ref like segments are, or compact covered ancestry). Keep fork replay output stable, and add a long-session regression test.

issue.creation_reason: Found while diagnosing the bob-cli-bc.4 monitor follow-up dead-end: the recorded authored request nests all fork ancestry, so long sessions will eventually exceed the 256 KiB validator cap and fail capture the same way.

payload.entry: Fixed by epic sase-1sd phase .4: sase commit 1087ccd7f1 carries the local pre-fork authored request through launch provenance (workflow_executor_steps_prompt_prepare, agent_delta, prompt), so captures stop re-nesting fork ancestry. A 20-cycle regression (test_launch_local_capture_chain.py) keeps the authored field under 262144 bytes. Sase-core fae59b46 reports authored-request byte limits. An over-cap starter now gets an explicit 'authored_local_request is too large' error that requires a bounded checkpoint via sase monitor resume -k FILE (monitor/resume.py, _settlement_followup.py, docs monitor-operations.md). The lander verified the source.
